draft.title: The nervous system
card: The nervous system is made of neurons, which are cells that carry messages as electrical impulses. Impulses travel very fast.
Sensory neurons carry impulses from receptors to the brain and spinal cord. Motor neurons carry impulses from the brain and spinal cord to effectors, such as muscles.
In most responses, the impulse goes to the brain, which decides what to do. This takes a little longer.
A reflex is a fast, automatic response. The impulse is passed on in the spinal cord without going to the brain first, so the effector acts sooner.
draft.remember: Neurons carry fast impulses, and a reflex is quicker because it skips the brain.

a.q: Which describes what a motor neuron does?
opts: Carries impulses from the spinal cord to a muscle
Carries impulses from a receptor to the spinal cord
Carries hormones from a gland to the blood
Carries impulses from the brain to a receptor
a.why: A motor neuron carries impulses to an effector such as a muscle. Carrying impulses from a receptor to the spinal cord is the job of a sensory neuron, which is the most tempting mix-up.
a.clue: Motor neurons lead to the part that responds.

b.q: Sam steps on a sharp shell on a beach in Perth and his foot jerks up before he feels pain. Why was the response so quick?
opts: The impulse was passed on in the spinal cord, not the brain
The impulse travelled faster along the neurons than normal
The foot detected the shell without using a receptor
The brain sent a stronger impulse to the leg muscles
b.why: In a reflex, the impulse is passed on in the spinal cord without going to the brain first, which shortens the path. The impulses do not travel faster, and a receptor is still needed to detect the shell.
b.clue: Think about the path the impulse takes, not its speed.

a.best: Carries impulses from the spinal cord to a muscle

b.best: The impulse was passed on in the spinal cord, not the brain
